title: Fix the Direct Instantiation of an Abstract Class
description: The program should create a concrete Circle shape and print its area.
expectedBehavior: The program should print the area of a concrete shape, such as a circle.
actualProblem: Shape is declared abstract and cannot be instantiated directly with new Shape() — the compiler rejects this with 'Shape is abstract; cannot be instantiated'.
explanation: An abstract class exists to be extended, not instantiated directly — it may have unimplemented (abstract) methods with no body. A concrete subclass, like Circle, must implement those methods before an object can actually be created.
